To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have derived an instantaneous vector representation for delta pitch which is amenable to acoustic modeling techniques and (2) using a small amount of manually labeled data, we have trained a system which outperforms current state-of-the art pause-only systems, achieving a recall of 0.95 and a precision of 0.92.

we have developed a novel acoustic representation that allows us to train a model to predict speaker change with a precision and recall that is comparable to the state-of-the-art and that we can control the model to predict speaker changes with a higher recall or a higher precision.

we have: 1) proposed a new acoustic model for predicting speaker change in spoken dialogue systems; 2) evaluated this model on a large corpus of real human-human dialogues, showing significant improvements in performance over current state-of-the art systems; and 3) demonstrated the ability of this model to be used for run-time control of speaker change prediction.

the design of a robust system for speaker-change prediction, and the demonstration of a new approach to acoustic modeling for conversational dialogue systems.
